content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I have 10 digital inputs (220 V AC), 3 analog inputs (pt100 sensors), and 4 outputs. Is it possible to use [product_name]230 with additional modules for this setup? My intended configuration is: [product_name]230RC > [product_name] DM8 230R > [product_name] AM2 pt100 > [product_name] AM2 pt100

Hello [user_name], Yes, you can use this configuration, but there are some important considerations: 1) Check if all 220 V AC inputs are from the same phase (L1, L2, or L3). If not, only 4 inputs from the same phase can be connected to each 'group' of digital inputs. On the 230RC, the first 4 inputs (I1 to I4) are physically separated from the next 4 (I5 to I8) to ensure isolation between different phases. 2) When using a DM 8 module for additional digital inputs, all inputs should be from the same phase. For a DM 16 module, you’ll notice inputs are split into 2 groups, allowing for different phases. If all inputs are from the same source, you don't need to group them by phase. 3) The base module (CPU) supports 4 outputs (10A relays) directly. Additional outputs (5A each) on the DM 8 module can be used as needed for other functions. 4) The 10A and 5A relay ratings apply to resistive loads like heating elements or regular light bulbs. For inductive loads (like motors), the current capacity is reduced. 5) The [product_name] Contact 230 provides excellent performance for loads up to 20A (resistive) and 4kW (inductive), offering reliability and good value compared to alternative brands. Hope this helps with your power project! [user_name]

Understood. [product_name]230RC L, N powered through UPS: - Inputs I1 to I6: Phase L1 - Outputs Q1-Q2: Phase L1 - Outputs Q3-Q4: Phase L2 (reserve) [product_name] DM8 230 L, N powered through UPS: - Inputs I1-I4: Phase L2 (reserve)

Hello [user_name], This configuration is well thought out. The relay outputs are potential-free, allowing each to be supplied independently. They are sufficiently isolated from one another, so you can even mix different phases on adjacent outputs without issue. Aaaaarggh! ("have a nice day!" from [user_name])

analysis.insight_summary: Users are verifying the suitability of a proposed hardware setup involving [product_name]230RC and its expansion modules for managing multiple AC inputs, analog sensors, and relay outputs. Discussions highlight electrical safety concerns, phase management across input groups, relay limitations depending on load type, and isolation features of the hardware. Users are focused on matching hardware capabilities to electrical requirements of their application, ensuring both reliability and compliance.

They are seeking confirmation that their chosen configuration is appropriate and compatible with the hardware specifications.
